valuation.price_action: stock up ~110% year-to-date on robotics/automation theme enthusiasm; was -75% from its listing-era high before that

analyst_reports.business_description: Vendor of software-orchestrated warehouse robotics ('robotics-as-a-service') for mid-size logistics and retail distribution customers. Founder-CEO is a charismatic serial entrepreneur with one prior billion-dollar exit. The company rebranded two years ago to emphasize 'autonomous AI robotics'. Stock-based compensation runs ~70% of revenue.
recent_developments: Revenue growth collapsed from +39% to +7% in one year, coinciding with a switch from upfront-license to per-pick consumption pricing (management frames the deceleration as a temporary transition artifact).
A single third-party-logistics joint-venture partner has historically accounted for ~28% of revenue; disclosed 'deployments' definitions have been questioned by analysts.
A short-seller report this year alleged that a large unbilled receivable from a related-party integrator overstates revenue; the company denies wrongdoing and its auditor signed the accounts.
Management announced a new 'foundation-model-driven autonomy' product suite; the stock more than doubled year-to-date as investors sought pure-play automation exposure.
Management withdrew its prior 'non-GAAP profitable by FY-end' target; guidance implies continued heavy losses.
analyst_reports.macro_context: Post-tightening de-rating in unprofitable tech, with a violent year-to-date rally in anything automation/AI branded.
